The fact that each appliance can be turned on or off without changing the voltage or current available to the others shows that each has its own independent path to the power source. In a **parallel** connection every device is connected across the same two supply points, so each receives the full line voltage regardless of what the other devices are doing. In a series connection the current would be the same through all devices and turning one off would interrupt the circuit for the rest, which is not observed. Whether the supply is AC or DC is irrelevant to this independence; it is the parallel wiring that guarantees it.

**Final answer: (C)**
